items.answer: Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Mixed reality, in a broad sense, is the entire space between the real environment extreme and the virtual environment extreme of the reality-virtuality continuum, containing different degrees of augmentation of the real environment with virtual content and of the virtual environment with real content.

Extended Reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).

In the development of computer systems, people have tried to make technology disappear from the user's point of view, and the current stage defined by popular technological products such as wearable devices, mobile devices, flexible devices, and connected devices is referred to as Internet of Things (IoT) or ubiquitous computing, in which users are surrounded by multiple connected computers that can communicate with each other without the user separately operating them, moving toward making technology disappear.

data.text: Computer vision is an enabling technology with huge potential for building better applications in augmented reality (AR) and mixed reality (MR). Cloud and edge computing concepts are relevant for scalable and affordable extended reality systems and for addressing resource optimization concerns. Machine learning and deep learning concepts are currently ubiquitous for building better experiences and more intelligent systems. Large language models (LLMs) or generative artificial intelligence (AI) can be used for enhanced interactivity, while IoT, robotics, and blockchain technology are relevant technologies for extended reality applications.

items.reason: Internet of Things, robotics, and blockchain are technologies relevant to extended reality applications, while resource optimization is named as a concern to be addressed rather than a relevant technology.

questions.question: How do cloud and edge computing relate to resource optimization and affordability in extended reality systems?
questions.reference_answer: Extended reality is an umbrella term covering immersive technologies such as augmented reality, virtual reality, and mixed reality. Cloud and edge computing are relevant for making such extended reality systems scalable and affordable, and for addressing resource optimization concerns.

questions.question: How does computer vision relate to the way augmented reality and mixed reality combine real and virtual content?
questions.reference_answer: Augmented reality is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content, while mixed reality broadly spans the space between the real and virtual extremes. Computer vision is an enabling technology with huge potential for building better applications in both augmented and mixed reality.

questions.question: How can machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and generative artificial intelligence change the experience and interactivity of extended reality systems?
questions.reference_answer: Machine learning and deep learning are currently ubiquitous for building better experiences and more intelligent systems in extended reality. Large language models or generative artificial intelligence can be used for enhanced interactivity in extended reality applications.

questions.question: How do the Internet of Things, robotics, and blockchain relate to extended reality applications, and how does the Internet of Things connect to making technology disappear?
questions.reference_answer: The Internet of Things, robotics, and blockchain are relevant technologies for extended reality applications. The Internet of Things is the current ubiquitous-computing stage in which users are surrounded by multiple connected computers that communicate with each other without the user separately operating them, moving toward making technology disappear.
